correctness.rationale: For even b>=4, sign Bernoulli convolution has Fourier product F_b(t)=product_j cos(2pi t/b^j), and canonical frequency digits lambda=(b/4)sum a_j b^j give an orthonormal exponential basis at depth m by the first differing binary digit (odd factor yields cos(pi*odd/2)=0). Conditioning on a cylinder produces cross Gram K=diag(F_b(lambda/b^m)) B where the finite prefix matrix B is exactly unitary by the same Hadamard argument; hence all principal cosines are the listed positive diagonal factors. F_b is strictly decreasing on [0,tau_b], so the unique worst equals F_b(tau_b(1-b^-m)), sharp projector gap sqrt(1-beta_m^2), and first-order level correction follow. Digit reversal couples empirical lambda/b^m to infinite T_b with O(b^-m) uniform distance, giving a Lipschitz test-function convergence bound. The digit Cantor set has Hausdorff dimension log2/log b<1 and F_b is Lipschitz injective, so limit measure is singular and atomless. First cosine factor yields large-base expansion 1-beta_b=pi²/[8(b-1)²]+O(b^-4). Fresh independent cross-Gram SVD/unity checks corroborated bases and levels; all-depth proofs are exact.
